You are working in the Go repository at /gin (the gin web framework v1.8.1, checked out at a commit that contains deliberately injected bugs). Your job: find and fix ONE bug in the file /gin/errors.go.

Context: a hidden test `TestErrorUnwrap` (package gin) currently fails because of this bug. The copy of TestErrorUnwrap that exists in /gin/errors_test.go does NOT check the buggy behavior (it passes), so you must reason about the intended behavior from the repository itself. The doc comment on the Unwrap method says: "Unwrap returns the wrapped error, to allow interoperability with errors.Is(), errors.As() and errors.Unwrap()". The gin `Error` type must therefore behave correctly with errors.Is / errors.As / errors.Unwrap in every reasonable usage: when a *Error is used directly, when an Error VALUE (not pointer) is used, when it is wrapped with fmt.Errorf("%w", ...), and when errors are nested.

Method: read /gin/errors.go carefully and compare every method (Error, Unwrap, IsType, SetType, SetMeta, JSON, MarshalJSON, and the errorMsgs methods) against its documented contract and against the semantics of the standard library errors package. Write throwaway tests (e.g. /gin/zz_tmp_unwrap_test.go) that exercise errors.Is/errors.As/errors.Unwrap on gin.Error in many forms (pointer, value, nested, wrapped by fmt.Errorf) to find the failing case. DELETE the throwaway file when you are done.

Constraints:
- Only edit /gin/errors.go. Do NOT edit, add or delete any pre-existing *_test.go file of the repo.
- Make the minimal fix; do not refactor, do not add features.
- At the end `cd /gin && go test ./...` must pass for all packages.
- Do not consult any other version of gin (no internet, no module-cache copies of other gin versions).

Report back: the exact bug (file, line, code before/after), the failing case you reproduced, and the final `go test ./...` output.

You are working in the Go repository at /gin (the gin web framework v1.8.1, checked out at a commit that contains deliberately injected bugs). Your job: find and fix TWO bugs, both in the file /gin/tree.go.

Context: two hidden tests currently fail because of them:
1. `TestRouteParamsNotEmpty` (package gin): it concerns the URL parameters (Params) produced by (*node).getValue for a matching route. The returned params must be correct and non-empty for routes with :params and *catch-all, including when the lookup has to roll back to a previously skipped node (see the skippedNodes / globalParamsCount logic) and when a wildcard follows a named parameter. A likely symptom is that for some matching route value.params ends up nil or empty (or truncated too far) even though the route matched.
2. `TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard` (package gin): it concerns (*node).findCaseInsensitivePath / findCaseInsensitivePathRec. The case-insensitive lookup must find the right path (with correct casing) when a node has multiple children and a wildcard child (param or catch-all), and must handle trailing-slash fixing.

The copies of these tests that exist in /gin/tree_test.go do NOT check the buggy behavior (they pass), so reason from the documented behavior of the router (see the comments in /gin/tree.go, /gin/path.go and the routing section of /gin/README.md) and from how the tree is built by addRoute/insertChild.

Method: read /gin/tree.go carefully, especially getValue, the skippedNode rollback blocks, the param/catchAll branches, and findCaseInsensitivePathRec. Write throwaway tests in /gin/zz_tmp_tree_test.go (DELETE it when done) that build trees with addRoute (see the helpers in tree_test.go such as fakeHandler, getParams, getSkippedNodes, checkRequests) and call getValue / findCaseInsensitivePath directly, reproducing failures. Also verify end-to-end with a gin engine if useful.

Constraints:
- Only edit /gin/tree.go. Do NOT edit, add or delete any pre-existing *_test.go file of the repo.
- Make minimal fixes; do not refactor, do not add features.
- At the end `cd /gin && go test ./...` must pass for all packages (tree_test.go, routes_test.go, gin_test.go etc. must all still pass).
- Do not consult any other version of gin (no internet, no module-cache copies of other gin versions).

Report back: for each bug, the exact location, code before/after, the failing case you reproduced, and the final `go test ./...` output.

You are working in the Go repository at /gin (the gin web framework v1.8.1, checked out at a commit that contains deliberately injected bugs). Your job: find and fix ONE bug in the file /gin/context.go.

Context: a hidden test `TestContextNegotiationFormat2` (package gin) currently fails because of this bug. The copy of the negotiation test that exists in /gin/context_test.go (TestContextNegotiationFormat) does NOT check the buggy behavior (it passes). The hidden test concerns content negotiation: Context.NegotiateFormat, Context.Negotiate, the helpers parseAccept / filterFlags / chooseData in /gin/utils.go, and the MIME constants in /gin/context.go. Check carefully how the Accept header is parsed and matched (exact matches, wildcards like */* and application/*, q-values/parameters, empty or malformed Accept headers, the fallback when nothing matches, and the documented behavior in the comments of NegotiateFormat/Negotiate).

Method: read /gin/context.go (and /gin/utils.go) carefully and compare the implementation with its documented contract. Write throwaway tests in /gin/zz_tmp_neg_test.go (DELETE it when done) that call c.NegotiateFormat with many Accept headers and formats (including "*/*", "application/*", "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8", empty header, headers with parameters) and find the case where the result is wrong.

Constraints:
- Only edit /gin/context.go (and, only if strictly necessary, /gin/utils.go). Do NOT edit, add or delete any pre-existing *_test.go file of the repo.
- Make the minimal fix; do not refactor, do not add features.
- At the end `cd /gin && go test ./...` must pass for all packages.

You are working in the Go repository at /gin (the gin web framework v1.8.1, checked out at a commit that contains deliberately injected bugs). Your job: find and fix ONE bug in the file /gin/response_writer.go.

Context: a hidden test `TestResponseWriterStatusCode` (package gin) currently fails because of this bug. The tests that exist in /gin/response_writer_test.go do NOT check the buggy behavior (they pass). Reason from the documented contract inside the file (the ResponseWriter interface comments) and from the standard library's http.ResponseWriter semantics: Status() must return the HTTP response status code of the current request, Written() must report whether the body/header was already written, WriteHeaderNow() must force writing the status code and headers, WriteHeader(code) must set the status code (ignoring non-positive codes), reset() must restore the initial state (size not written, status 200), Size() must report the number of bytes written, Write/WriteString must write the header first and count the bytes, Flush/Hijack/Pusher/CloseNotify must delegate.

Method: read /gin/response_writer.go carefully. Write throwaway tests in /gin/zz_tmp_rw_test.go that cover many status-code scenarios (WriteHeader with various codes including 0 and negative, WriteHeaderNow, Write, WriteString, Flush, Hijack, reset, calling WriteHeader twice, calling WriteHeader after the header was already written, using httptest.NewRecorder and a real httptest.NewServer) and find the scenario where the observed behavior is wrong. DELETE the throwaway file when you are done.
